description: Cyprien Hoelzl publishes railFE, a Python model of vertical interaction between a simplified railway vehicle and track. It represents rails with Timoshenko beam elements on discrete sleeper supports and couples a quarter-car representation through nonlinear Hertzian wheel–rail contact. The repository documents state-space matrices, frequency-response calculations and examples with track irregularities. Zenodo archives version 1.0.0 from February 2023; its generic open-licence label is clarified by the linked repository’s MIT licence. The model is freely downloadable for vehicle–track dynamic simulations. It is geographically transferable, not a calibrated representation of a particular railway. Applicability to full vehicle dynamics and field-validation accuracy remain unknown from the inspected documentation. No related catalogue record explicitly covers railFE. The README identifies railfe2 as a later extension, which is not assumed identical. Code was not executed.
